subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, routing & tiering) - Acme Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Smith <alice.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, routing & tiering) - Acme Health

Hi Alice / team,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we all have the same baseline and next steps. Please flag anything I got wrong or missed.

Pain points you shared:
- No reliable per-customer rate limiting: bursts from a few tenants are impacting others (noisy neighbor).
- Limited ability to enforce quotas or tiering per plan (basic/premium/enterprise).
- Need per-customer routing/policies (e.g., route enterprise to dedicated capacity, lower tiers to shared).
- Difficulty with billing/usage alignment because usage metering is coarse and not tied to tenants.
- Regulatory concerns (HIPAA adjacency) — need stronger audit logs and tenant segregation for sensitive workloads.

Current stack you described:
- AWS-hosted services behind Envoy; traffic shaping done mostly at API gateway layer.
- In-house routing layer that isn’t tied into model serving decisions.
- No central model for tenant-level quota enforcement today.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- Ability to set and enforce per-tenant rate limits (qps and token limits) with clear SLA behaviors.
- Quotas and tiering that map cleanly to billing (per-tenant metering exports).
- Policy-based routing so we can pin premium customers to dedicated instances/regions.
- Audit logs for all inference requests and config changes.
- Proof-of-concept/pilot where 5–10 tenants are onboarded with enforcement and billing integration.

What Redwood can deliver (high-level):
- Per-customer rate-limiting primitives (qps + token caps) configurable per-route + plan.
- Quota enforcement and metering exports (CSV/BigQuery) that map to tenant IDs for billing.
- Smart routing policies: route by tenant tag to dedicated pools, fallback to shared with graceful degradation.
- Prefix/KV caching and tenant-aware batching to minimize cross-tenant interference.
- Audit logs and integration points for SIEM/KMS for sensitive workloads.

Open questions for the deep-dive:
- Do you require enforcement at the edge (Envoy) or is enforcement inside the Redwood runtime acceptable?
- Expected qps/token distribution per tenant (we asked for a sample traffic matrix).
- Which tenants need dedicated isolation vs. shared but throttled?

Next steps:
1) I’ll send a short discovery recap doc + a sample multi-tenancy config template (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Marissa) and product engineer (Sean) — 60 minutes to walk configs and demo routing.
3) You to share a traffic sample (CSV) and a prioritized list of 5–10 tenants for the pilot.
4) Security/compliance checklist: we’ll share SOC2 and our audit log examples; you to indicate HIPAA controls needed.

Proposed time for deep-dive: Thu 3/11 10:00–11:00am PT or Fri 3/12 9:00–10:00am PT — please confirm what works best.

Attachments: discovery-recap-acme.pdf (one-pager), multi-tenancy-controls-template.yaml (config example).

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Alice Smith <alice.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, routing & tiering) - Acme Health

Thanks Ben — this is great and captures the key points. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Enforcement: we'd prefer enforcement as close to runtime as possible; if Redwood can enforce in the serving layer that works, but we may still want Envoy-level knobs for emergency throttles.
- Traffic sample: attached a small CSV with tenant_id, hourly_requests, avg_token_length for the last 7 days. (see eng@acmehealth.com)
- Isolation candidates: We have 3 enterprise tenants that need dedicated capacity, ~20 midsize tenants that need stricter quotas, and a long tail of small tenants.
- Compliance: we are not fully HIPAA-covered yet but any tenant processing PHI will need audit trails and possibly KMS integration.

Deep-dive: Thu 3/11 10:00am PT works for our engineers (I'll send calendar invite).

Quick ask: can you include an example of per-tenant billing export column names so our billing team can validate?

Appreciate it — Alice
Alice Smith
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Health
alice.smith@acmehealth.com
